title: Glynis W Probable NDE 7461
content: August 1, 1991, I was having 1650 cc’s of fluid removed from my right lung through my back by thoracentesis hooked up to a pump. I was sitting up in a chair with some sort of bar for which I could lean. As the fluid was being removed, I felt a strange pressure in the brain stem, and then around my heart. My body went limp; my shoes fell off as I started to sweat profusely. I heard the surgeon talking about removing the tube as a bright light appeared up and off to the right. There was a peaceful feeling and I knew I would go to heaven. I was rushed out of that room and put on my bed. As my mother rushed to my side, the nurses took my blood pressure. My mother yelled out, '70/30.' Although I was lying on the bed, I could see my mother talking to my doctor in the doorway as he told her, 'I hope we can get her back!' That is the last thing I remember until waking up with a team of doctors around me and I was soaking wet. The nurses kept asking me after the experience if I saw a tunnel or people. I knew who had passed on. I did not. But strange things started happening. I called my grandmother after entering the hospital and told her I was in trouble. She took the pray warriors in order to fast and pray for me that it wasn't cancer. It turned out to be endometriosis. [Editor’s note: Endometriosis is the abnormal growth of cells similar to those that form inside the uterus, but in a location outside the uterus.] I was discharged from the hospital on August 28, 1991, and arrived at my grandmother's house. She told me that she asked God to take her if he needed another soldier in heaven and leave me here to be a help to the nation. She had a cerebral hemorrhage the next day. She had informed everyone at church Sunday, before I arrived, that she was going home on Thursday. February 9, 1998, in South Korea: My right lung collapsed (hemopneumothorax) and my chest tube suction became disconnected while traveling back from a CAT scan at the army hospital, two hours away. A severe blizzard caused emergency road conditions. As I became progressively more short of breath, we began to hear a strange noise, but could not find anything wrong. I began to panic as I gasped for breath. Up on the glass cabinet in the ambulance, I saw the wings of my guardian angel. I heard the words, 'Relax, don’t panic, relax.' As I relaxed, I realized it was not the technician talking. Many wondered how I survived out there. I know it was an angel. My last NDE was in May 30, 2002. I had a full tension pneumothorax, decompression of my chest, two minutes from death but I never lost consciousness. But the situation surrounding the event was very strange. I realized I had been chosen by God to deliver the message about Catamenial Pneumothorax. My purpose became clear. [Editor’s Note: Catamenial Pneumothorax is the most common form of thoracic endometriosis syndrome.]

boundary_and_return.mission_detail: She reports being "chosen by God to deliver the message about Catamenial Pneumothorax" and that her "purpose became clear."

context.nde_cause_other_detail: 1991 thoracentesis with severe hypotension/near arrest; 1998 hemopneumothorax with chest tube suction disconnected; 2002 tension pneumothorax with decompression.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: 1998: saw "the wings of my guardian angel" and heard "Relax, don’t panic, relax." 1991: reported seeing her mother and doctor from bed and a bright light "up and off to the right."
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: 1991: bright light appeared while hearing surgeon; later she reports seeing her mother and doctor in doorway while lying on bed; then loss of memory until waking with doctors around. 1998: angel wings seen and calming words heard during respiratory crisis.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: She reports multiple episodes described as NDEs/probable NDEs across 1991, 1998, and 2002; in 2002 she states she was "two minutes from death" but "never lost consciousness."
unique_elements.notable_quotes: 1991: "There was a peaceful feeling and I knew I would go to heaven." Doctor: "I hope we can get her back!" 1998: "Relax, don’t panic, relax." 2002: "I realized I had been chosen by God to deliver the message about Catamenial Pneumothorax."
